questions.question: Explain why plywood is less likely to warp than solid timber of the same thickness.

points.text: Solid timber has grain in one direction - it warps along the grain as moisture changes. Plywood's alternating veneer layers create opposing grain directions that cancel out warping forces.

questions.question: A designer is making a kitchen worktop. Compare solid oak and MDF, justifying your recommendation.

points.text: Solid oak: beautiful grain, very durable, water-resistant with treatment - but expensive, can warp, heavy. MDF: smooth, uniform, does not warp, affordable - but swells if water penetrates, cannot be refinished.

questions.question: Discuss the environmental advantages and disadvantages of using hardwoods in product design.

points.text: Advantages: durable (products last decades), repairable, biodegradable, carbon-neutral if sustainably sourced. Disadvantages: slow growth, deforestation risk, high transport miles, illegal logging concerns. FSC certification helps.
